draft.title: Surface area and volume
card: A prism has the same cross-section (base) all the way along. Volume of a prism = base area × height, where height is the distance between the two ends.
Surface area is the total area of every face of a solid. Add the areas of all the faces, including the two ends.
Volume is in cubic units such as cm³. Surface area is in square units such as cm².
draft.remember: Volume is base area × height in cubic units. Surface area adds every face in square units.

a.q: A prism has a base area of 12 cm² and a height of 7 cm. What is its volume?
a.why: Volume = base area × height = 12 × 7 = 84 cm³. Adding 12 and 7 gives 19, which mixes up the operation. Volume is measured in cubic units, so cm² is wrong.
a.clue: Multiply the base area by the height.

b.q: A closed box measures 6 cm by 2 cm by 5 cm. What is its surface area?
b.why: The faces are 2 × (6×2) + 2 × (6×5) + 2 × (2×5) = 24 + 60 + 20 = 104 cm². Finding 6 × 2 × 5 = 60 gives the volume, not the surface area. Using each face type only once gives 52, which skips the pairs of faces.
b.clue: A box has three pairs of matching faces.

check.summary: No problems found. The card, the worked example (60 cm³ and 94 cm²) and both answers (84 cm³ and 104 cm²) check out, and the distractors reflect common errors.

final.title: Surface area and volume
card: A prism has the same cross-section (base) all the way along. Volume of a prism \(=\) base area \(\times\) height, where height is the distance between the two ends.
Surface area is the total area of every face of a solid. Add the areas of all the faces, including the two ends.
Volume is in cubic units such as \(\text{cm}^{3}\). Surface area is in square units such as \(\text{cm}^{2}\).

A box is 5 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm. Volume \(= (5 \times 3) \times 4 = 60\text{ cm}^{3}\). Faces: \(2 \times (5 \times 3)\), \(2 \times (5 \times 4)\) and \(2 \times (3 \times 4)\) give \(30 + 40 + 24 = 94\text{ cm}^{2}\).
final.remember: Volume is base area \(\times\) height in cubic units. Surface area adds every face in square units.

a.q: A prism has a base area of \(12\text{ cm}^{2}\) and a height of 7 cm. What is its volume?
a.why: Volume \(=\) base area \(\times\) height \(= 12 \times 7 = 84\text{ cm}^{3}\). Adding 12 and 7 gives 19, which mixes up the operation. Volume is measured in cubic units, so \(\text{cm}^{2}\) is wrong.
a.clue: Multiply the base area by the height.

b.q: A closed box measures 6 cm by 2 cm by 5 cm. What is its surface area?
b.why: The faces are \(2 \times (6 \times 2)\), \(2 \times (6 \times 5)\) and \(2 \times (2 \times 5)\), which give \(24 + 60 + 20 = 104\text{ cm}^{2}\). Finding \(6 \times 2 \times 5 = 60\) gives the volume, not the surface area. Using each face type only once gives 52, which skips the pairs of faces.
b.clue: A box has three pairs of matching faces.
